details: Minutes from the October Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, released on November 18, revealed strong support among policymakers for further interest rate increases to combat persistent inflation. Nearly all officials agreed that additional hikes would likely be appropriate, with some even considering a rise of more than 25 basis points in December. This hawkish outlook makes non-interest-bearing assets like cryptocurrencies less attractive to investors.
title: Fed's Hawkish Stance Boosts Rate Hike Odds, Dampens Crypto Appeal

details: The blockbuster market debut of AI firm Anthropic on November 19, the largest IPO on record, initially saw its shares surge. However, this optimism quickly faded, and US stock indexes, particularly in the tech sector, tumbled. The IPO's failure to rekindle enthusiasm for AI-related stocks, coupled with ongoing concerns about high spending on AI infrastructure and recent issues with Nvidia, contributed to a broader market risk-off sentiment.
title: Anthropic IPO Falls Flat, Triggers Broader Market Sell-off

details: The total supply of major stablecoins has seen a substantial drop of $14.2 billion over the past 30 days, marking the largest contraction since the 2022 crypto bear market. This reduction, particularly in USDT and USDC, indicates that holders are redeeming stablecoins for traditional fiat currency and withdrawing cash from the market. This trend suggests reduced buying power and less capital available to fuel a cryptocurrency rally.
title: Stablecoin Supply Drops Significantly, Signaling Crypto Outflows
